policies.title: Afghan, North Korean and Palestinian ordinary passports: sponsored Oman tourist eVisa
policies.summary: Oman's Royal Oman Police states that tourists of all nationalities may obtain a sponsored 30-day tourist visa. ROP's eVisa FAQ lists sponsored tourist visas in the eVisa system and confirms electronic delivery after approval.
conditions: A tourism company licensed to practise tourism activities in Oman must sponsor the tourist application; this is not an unsponsored passport-only entitlement, visa exemption, or visa on arrival.

The government service states a 30-day visa, extendable for a similar period. The ROP FAQ identifies sponsored tourist visas as eVisa-system products and says an approved visa is sent electronically to the registered email before travel.

The applicant must present a normal passport with at least six months' validity and meet sponsor, application, security, carrier, border-control and final-admission requirements. A submitted or paid application does not guarantee issue.
Work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, emergency, refugee, stateless and other special-document routes remain outside this short-tourist finding.

application.label: Royal Oman Police eVisa service
application.processingTime: ROP recommends lodging a complete eVisa application at least four days in advance; individual processing times may vary.
steps: Arrange sponsorship through an Oman-licensed tourism company.
Submit the sponsored tourist application through the Royal Oman Police eVisa system with the required normal-passport data and supporting material.
Wait for approval and retain the electronic visa delivered to the registered email before travel.

No current Panamanian primary source directly maps an ordinary Timor-Leste passport to visitor eligibility and an issuance route. Omission and the separate third-country-document waiver are excluded.
Panama's schedule names Sudan but not the distinct state of South Sudan. No current authority supplies a South Sudanese ordinary-passport result; no predecessor-name or complement inference is made.

Current Chinese guidance makes Mainland access depend on resident/citizenship status and a Mainland Travel Permit or PRC Travel Document. It does not yield one Hong Kong SAR ordinary-passport visitor status or issuance point.

Current Chinese guidance makes Mainland access depend on resident/citizenship status and a Mainland Travel Permit or PRC Travel Document. It does not yield one Macao SAR ordinary-passport visitor status or issuance point.

Current Chinese guidance requires a Taiwan resident Mainland Travel Permit, with a PRC Travel Document mission route when travelling from abroad without one. This person/document scheme cannot be normalized as a Taiwan ordinary-passport visitor visa or arrival visa.

Hong Kong's current arrangements distinguish Macao permanent/non-permanent resident documentation from a Macao SAR passport, which receives only qualifying seven-day transit treatment. No passport-wide visitor baseline follows.

Current PAR and entry-permit routes depend on Taiwan residence, birthplace or prior admission, permitted documents and other personal facts. They do not establish one Taiwan ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline.
Hong Kong's current foreign-visitor dataset supplies no direct ordinary Kosovo-passport result. Its residual row is not used to infer recognition, a waiver or visa issuance timing.
